title: Sen. Lisa Murkowski addresses Trump's statements and highlights advocacy for ALS patients

Sen. Lisa Murkowski addresses Trump’s statements and highlights advocacy for ALS patients
Sen.
Sen. Lisa Murkowski, Alaska's senior senator and the first woman elected to represent the state in the U.S. Senate, addressed a range of policy issues in a series of posts on September 29 and 30, 2026.
On September 29, Murkowski commented on recent remarks by former President Trump regarding cultural landmarks, stating, "President Trump has made recent statements about the Kennedy Center and the ‘Triumphal Arch,’ giving very little context or content about either to Congress or the public. Any action to demolish facilities authorized by Congress or to construct facilities on federal land first" (posted at 16:35 UTC).
Later that day, she highlighted challenges faced by individuals with ALS and emphasized ongoing support for research efforts: "For those living with ALS, every day matters. They cannot afford disruptions in research, treatment access, and support. This reauthorization ensures that the momentum we have built over the past five years will continue, keeping pathways to promising investigational treatments" (posted at 21:24 UTC).
On September 30, Murkowski marked Orange Shirt Day—the National Day of Remembrance for Indian Boarding School Survivors—by posting: "On Orange Shirt Day, the National Day of Remembrance for Indian Boarding School Survivors, we honor the children who returned home and remember those who never did." (posted at 19:08 UTC).
Murkowski is known for her support of Alaska Native communities and focus on state infrastructure needs (official website). She grew up in several Alaskan communities as a fourth-generation Alaskan and holds degrees from Georgetown University and Willamette University. In addition to her legislative work, she is married with two sons.
